audit.summary: The file formalizes Theorem 1.1 of the paper (Ehrhart's sharp volume inequality). For a convex, compact, full-dimensional set S ⊂ ℝⁿ with barycenter 0 and int(S) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}, it states vol(S) ≤ (n+1)ⁿ/n!. It also formalizes sharpness: the centered simplex (n+1)Δₙ − (1,…,1) has barycenter 0 and volume (n+1)ⁿ/n!, and some centered body attains the bound. The definitions match the standard notions. The only caveat is minor: no standalone theorem says that the centered simplex itself has 0 as its unique interior lattice point. That fact is only implied indirectly, through the existential sharpness theorem.

glossary.plain: ℝⁿ as Fin n → ℝ, with the Lebesgue (product) volume
Lebesgue volume of K as a real number (toReal; this is junk 0 only if the volume is infinite)
glossary.note: Despite the name, this is not normalized. It equals vol for compact K.
Junk values arise only if vol(K) = 0 or x is not integrable on K. Neither happens for compact, full-dimensional K.

glossary.plain: convex, compact, nonempty-interior K with barycenter 0 and int(K) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}

lean_claims.plain: For n > 0 and S ⊂ ℝⁿ convex, compact, with nonempty interior, barycenter 0, and int(S) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}: vol(S) ≤ (n+1)ⁿ/n!.
For all n, the barycenter of (n+1)Δₙ − 1 is 0.
For n > 0 there is a convex, compact, full-dimensional body with barycenter 0 and int ∩ ℤⁿ = {0} whose volume equals (n+1)ⁿ/n!.

paper_claims.plain: A full-dimensional compact convex K ⊂ ℝⁿ with barycenter 0 and int(K) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0} has vol(K) ≤ (n+1)ⁿ/n!.
The simplex (n+1)Δₙ − (1,…,1) has barycenter 0, has no interior lattice point other than 0, and has volume (n+1)ⁿ/n!.

coverage.why: The hypotheses and conclusion match. The n = 0 case is excluded, but it is trivial.
The existential theorem does not say the extremizer is the centered simplex. The barycenter and volume of the simplex are proved separately, but its lattice-point condition is not.

flags.explanation: There is no standalone statement that interiorLatticePoints (centeredSimplex n) = {0}. Sharpness is captured only existentially, so the witness need not be the simplex. This still suffices for sharpness of the bound.

lint_verdicts.why: In every target use, the set is compact and full-dimensional (or n = 0, where the point has measure 1). So the volume is positive and finite and x is integrable on it.
n! is never 0, so the real division is genuine.
This is the same constant, and n! ≠ 0.

theorem probe_n1 : Ehrhart.interiorLatticePoints (Ehrhart.centeredSimplex 1) = {0} := by
  have h : Ehrhart.centeredSimplex 1 = Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-1:ℝ) 1) := by
    ext x
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨y, ⟨h0, hs⟩, rfl⟩ i _
      have h1 := h0 0
      simp at hs
      have : i = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
      subst this
      simp only [Ehrhart.simplexDilation, Set.mem_Icc]
      push_cast
      constructor <;> linarith
    · intro hx
      refine ⟨fun i => (x i + 1)/2, ⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
      · intro i
        have := (hx i trivial).1
        simp only
        linarith
      · have := (hx 0 trivial).2
        simp
        linarith
      · funext i
        simp [Ehrhart.simplexDilation]
        ring
  ext z
  simp only [Ehrhart.interiorLatticePoints, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  rw [h, interior_pi_set Set.finite_univ]
  simp only [Set.mem_pi, Set.mem_univ, true_implies, interior_Icc, Set.mem_Ioo]
  constructor
  · intro hz
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hz 0
    have a' : (-1:ℝ) < (z 0 : ℝ) := h1
    have b' : (z 0 : ℝ) < 1 := h2
    have a : -1 < z 0 := by exact_mod_cast a'
    have b : z 0 < 1 := by exact_mod_cast b'
    funext i
    have : i = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    subst this
    simp
    omega
  · rintro rfl i
    simp [Ehrhart.integerPoint]

result.claim: There is a concrete instance of Ehrhart.CenteredBody 0, with carrier the whole one-point space, so the structure's hypotheses (convex, compact, nonempty interior, barycenter 0, unique interior lattice point 0) can all be satisfied together. This is a degenerate dimension (n = 0) instance.

∀ {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (S : Set (Space n))
    (hconvex : Convex ℝ S)
    (hcompact : IsCompact S)
    (hinterior : (interior S).Nonempty)
    (hcentered : barycenter S = 0)
    (hlattice : interiorLatticePoints S = {0}), normalizedVolume S ≤
      ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ)
restatements.restated: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∀ S : Set (Fin n → ℝ), Convex ℝ S → IsCompact S → (interior S).Nonempty → barycenter S = 0 → {z : Fin n → ℤ | (fun i => (z i : ℝ)) ∈ interior S} = {0} → ((MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) S).toReal ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ)
restatements.english: For n ≥ 1, every convex compact set S in ℝⁿ with nonempty interior and barycenter 0, whose only interior integer lattice point is the origin, has Lebesgue volume at most (n+1)^n / n!.

namespace Ehrhart.Volume
open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal
theorem probe_restate_2  :
    (∀ {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (S : Set (Space n))
    (hconvex : Convex ℝ S)
    (hcompact : IsCompact S)
    (hinterior : (interior S).Nonempty)
    (hcentered : barycenter S = 0)
    (hlattice : interiorLatticePoints S = {0}), normalizedVolume S ≤
      ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ)) ↔
    (∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∀ S : Set (Fin n → ℝ), Convex ℝ S → IsCompact S → (interior S).Nonempty → barycenter S = 0 → {z : Fin n → ℤ | (fun i => (z i : ℝ)) ∈ interior S} = {0} → ((MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) S).toReal ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ)) := by
  exact Iff.rfl
end Ehrhart.Volume

namespace Ehrhart.SimplexVolume
open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal
theorem probe_restate_11  :
    (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n), ∃ K : CenteredBody n,
      normalizedVolume K.carrier = sharpConstant n) ↔
    (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ S : Set (Fin n → ℝ), Convex ℝ S ∧ IsCompact S ∧ (interior S).Nonempty ∧ barycenter S = 0 ∧ {z : Fin n → ℤ | (fun i => (z i : ℝ)) ∈ interior S} = {0} ∧ ((volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) S).toReal = ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ)) := by
  constructor
  · intro h n hn
    obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := h n hn
    exact ⟨K.carrier, K.convex, K.compact, K.fullDimensional, K.centered, K.uniqueInteriorLatticePoint, hK⟩
  · intro h n hn
    obtain ⟨S, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6⟩ := h n hn
    exact ⟨⟨S, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5⟩, h6⟩
end Ehrhart.SimplexVolume

restatements.restated: ∀ m : ℕ, Ehrhart.normalizedVolume (Ehrhart.centeredSimplex m) = 0 ∨ ∫ x in Ehrhart.centeredSimplex m, x ∂(volume : Measure (Ehrhart.Space m)) = 0
restatements.english: For every dimension m, either the centered simplex has volume zero, or the integral of the position vector x over it is the zero vector. This is what barycenter = 0 means once the scalar factor 1/volume is unfolded.
restatements.lean:
namespace Ehrhart.SimplexVolume
open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal
theorem probe_restate_21  :
    (∀ (n : ℕ), barycenter (centeredSimplex n) = 0) ↔
    (∀ m : ℕ, Ehrhart.normalizedVolume (Ehrhart.centeredSimplex m) = 0 ∨ ∫ x in Ehrhart.centeredSimplex m, x ∂(volume : Measure (Ehrhart.Space m)) = 0) := by
  simp only [Ehrhart.barycenter, smul_eq_zero, inv_eq_zero]
end Ehrhart.SimplexVolume
